This document provides a Quick Overview of most, but not all, functions
contained in the `PscanR` package, which is used for motif enrichment
analysis in promoter sequences.  
For a comprehensive reference, please consult the `PscanR` Reference Manual.

<hr />

## Table 1: PscanR main functions for Motif Enrichment Analysis

<table style="border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%;">
    <thead>
    <tr>
        <th style="width:20%; border-bottom: 2px solid #ccc;">Function</th>
        <th style="width:80%; border-bottom: 2px solid #ccc;">Description</th>
    </tr>
    </thead>
    <tbody>
    <tr>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;"><code>pscan()</code></td>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
    Scans a set of promoter sequences with motif matrices to compute the binding
    affinity scores and assesses motif enrichment against a background.
</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
    <code>pscan_fullBG()</code>
</td>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
    Uses a pre-computed full background containing the binding affinity scores
    for all promoters in the organism of study, and it retrieves the scores for
    the sequences in input (a subset of promoters) to avoid redundant
    calculation and speed up the analysis.
</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;"><code>PscanFiltered()</code></td>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
    Applies the Pscan algorithm to sequences filtered based on their affinity
    with a specific motif matrix, allowing focused analysis on relevant
    sequences.
</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;"><code>ps_select_promoters()</code></td>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
    Maps genes to transcript promoters and selects one representative promoter per gene, using a rule appropriate to the transcript identifier scheme in use. The scheme is detected automatically and reported, so the choice remains auditable.
</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;"><code>ps_selection_summary()</code></td>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
    Reports how a mapping produced by <code>ps_select_promoters()</code> was arrived at: which scheme was used, which rule selected each promoter, how many genes offered a real choice, and how many were decided by the tie-break rather than by the ranking.
</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td><code>ps_load_select_transcripts()</code></td>
        <td>
    Downloads and caches the human MANE Select and RefSeq Select transcript tables from UCSC hg38, for use as the ranking passed to <code>ps_select_promoters()</code>. This metadata is hg38-specific; for other organisms a species-specific table is supplied instead.
</td>
    </tr>
    </tbody>
</table>

<hr />

## Table 2: Background construction

We refer to ‘Background’ as the collection of scores obtained by
scanning any promoter sequence of the organism of study against the
set of motif matrices that are investigated for the motif enrichment
analysis (can be sourced from public databases such as JASPAR).

<table style="border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%;">
    <thead>
    <tr>
        <th style="width:30%; border-bottom: 2px solid #ccc;">Function</th>
        <th style="width:70%; border-bottom: 2px solid #ccc;">Description</th>
    </tr>
    </thead>
    <tbody>
    <tr>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
            <code>ps_build_bg()</code>
        </td>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
    Constructs the background by applying the pscan() algorithm to all annotated
    promoter sequences of the organism.
</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
    <code>generate_psmatrixlist_from_background()</code>
</td>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
    Retrieves pre-computed background.
</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
    <code>get_availableBG()</code>
</td>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
    Displays the names of all available precomputed backgrounds, with options to
    filter by keywords.
</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;"><code>ps_retrieve_bg_from_file()</code></td>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
    Generates a background from a text file containing background information
    for each matrix, including ID, background size, average score, and standard
    deviation.
</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;"><code>ps_build_bg_from_table()</code></td>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
    Associates background parameters held in a <code>data.frame</code> with a list of position frequency matrices and returns the result as a <code>PSMatrixList</code>.
</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;"><code>ps_get_bg_table()</code></td>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
    Extracts the background statistics (size, mean and standard deviation) from a <code>PSMatrixList</code> as a <code>data.frame</code>, which is the inverse of <code>ps_build_bg_from_table()</code>.
</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;"><code>ps_write_bg_to_file()</code></td>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
    Writes the background statistics of a <code>PSMatrixList</code> to a text file, in the format <code>ps_retrieve_bg_from_file()</code> reads back.
</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;"><code>ps_build_bg(fullBG = TRUE)</code></td>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
    Builds a <em>full</em> background instead of the three summary statistics per matrix. A full background retains, for every promoter and every matrix, the hit score, position, strand and matched oligonucleotide. It is far larger than a standard background, so none is shipped with the package.
</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;"><code>pscan_fullBG()</code></td>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
    The reason to build a full background. It scans a foreground given only <em>transcript identifiers</em>, retrieving hits already stored in the full background rather than rescanning DNA, which makes repeated foreground scans against one background very fast.
</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td><code>transcriptIDLegend()</code></td>
        <td>
    Retrieves the legend of a full background: the mapping from every original sequence name to the representative kept after de-duplication. It is what lets <code>pscan_fullBG()</code> resolve an identifier that was not itself retained.
</td>
    </tr>
    </tbody>
</table>

<hr />

## Table 3: Visualization of the results

<table style="border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%;">
    <thead>
    <tr>
        <th style="width:25%; border-bottom: 2px solid #ccc;">Function</th>
        <th style="width:85%; border-bottom: 2px solid #ccc;">Description</th>
    </tr>
    </thead>
    <tbody>
    <tr>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
    <code>ps_results_table()</code>
</td>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
    Displays a summary table of results, ordered by increasing p-values.
    Transcription factors can be filtered based on a specified false discovery
    rate (FDR) threshold.
</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
            <code>ps_z_table()</code>
        </td>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
    Creates a matrix of Z-scores for motif occurrences across multiple
    PSMatrices contained in a PSMatrixList.
</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
    <code>ps_zscore_heatmap()</code>
</td>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
    Generates a heatmap visualizing the correlation of Z-scores for
    transcription factors, based on a specified FDR threshold.
</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
    <code>ps_hitpos_map()</code>
</td>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
        Produces a heatmap showing the positional distribution of motif hits,
        aiding in the identification of common binding regions.
        </td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
    <code>ps_density_plot()</code>
</td>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
        Creates a density plot representing the distribution of hits along
        promoter sequences, based on their position and score for a specific
        position weight matrix (PWM).
        </td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;"><code>ps_hit_score_plot()</code></td>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
    Plots every promoter's best hit as a point positioned by where the site sits and by how well it scores, so that position and strength are read together. A positional profile alone cannot show whether a concentration is made of strong sites or of weak ones.
</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;"><code>ps_motif_barplot()</code></td>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
    Plots the highest ranking motifs of a scan as horizontal bars, optionally coloured by a grouping such as the structural class of the factor.
</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td><code>ps_motif_class()</code></td>
        <td>
    Returns the structural class of the transcription factor behind each motif, for example <code>"Basic leucine zipper factors (bZIP)"</code>. It supplies the grouping <code>ps_motif_barplot()</code> colours by.
</td>
    </tr>
    </tbody>
</table>
